questions.question: Which of the following could represent the graph of $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$?
questions.answer: $y = \dfrac1x$ is a hyperbola: two branches, in the first and third quadrants, never touching either axis. **(B)**

questions.question:
The resting heart rates in beats per minute (bpm) of 6 students were recorded in the table below.

| Heart rate | 55 | 72 | 72 | 76 | 78 | 79 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The resting rate of 55 bpm was incorrectly recorded and hence removed from the data. Which of the following measures will NOT change?
questions.answer: Removing 55 changes the mean, the median ($74 \to 76$) and the range ($24 \to 7$), but the mode stays 72. **(B)**

questions.question: What is 0.006082 expressed in standard form with three significant figures?

A distribution is shown below.

Which of the following box-and-whisker plots best represents the data distribution?
questions.answer: The distribution is negatively skewed (long tail to the left), so the box plot has a long left whisker and the median sits towards the right of the box. **(D)**

questions.question: The value of $P$ varies directly with $Q$. It is known that when $P = 4.5$, $Q = 13.5$. What is the value of $P$ when $Q = 42$?
The scale of a map is $1 : 25\,000$. A road is 6 cm long on the map. What is the actual length of the road?

The edges on the diagram below represent roads that link eight towns. It is possible for a garbage truck to drive along each road only once and thus not waste fuel. The garbage truck starts at Jamison and will travel along each road once. At which town will the garbage truck finish?
questions.answer: A route using every edge exactly once (an Euler trail) must start and finish at the two vertices of odd degree. Jamison and Clifton are the only odd-degree vertices, so starting at Jamison the truck finishes at Clifton. **(C)**

questions.question:
Suzan is paid at a rate of \$42.50 per hour for working casually from 2:00 pm until 6:00 pm each day, Monday to Friday. When working on a Sunday, Suzan is paid at time-and-a-half rate per hour.

During one week, Suzan worked Monday to Friday and Sunday. She was paid a total of \$1168.75 for that week's work.

How many hours did Suzan work on Sunday of this week?
Matt is in hospital and needs to receive 2.5 litres of antibiotic fluid over 5 hours. What is the required flow rate in mL/h?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{2500\text{ mL}}{5\text{ h}} = 500$ mL/h. **(C)**

questions.question:
Carmine has a credit card which has no interest-free period. Interest is charged at 19.5% per annum, compounding daily, on the amount owing.

At the start of the month Carmine had an opening balance of \$162, and during the month Carmine used his credit card to purchase a phone for \$700.

He was charged interest on the opening balance for 30 days and on the purchase of the phone for 24 days.

How much interest was Carmine charged for the month?
questions.answer:
Daily rate $= \dfrac{0.195}{365}$.
$$I = 162\left[\left(1 + \tfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{30} - 1\right] + 700\left[\left(1 + \tfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{24} - 1\right] \approx 2.62 + 9.03 = \$11.65. \quad \textbf{(A)}$$

questions.question:
A rugby fan in Perth (Australia) plans to watch a live match played in New Zealand next winter. The time zone for Perth is UTC +8. The time zone for New Zealand is UTC +13 in winter and UTC +12 in summer.

If the match is played at 6:30 pm New Zealand time, what time will the match be viewed in Perth?
questions.answer: In winter Perth is $13 - 8 = 5$ hours behind New Zealand: 6:30 pm $-$ 5 h $=$ 1:30 pm. **(A)**

questions.question:
The stem-and-leaf diagram below shows the distribution of the ages of 24 members of a committee.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 2 | $m$ |
| 3 | 2 2 3 7 8 8 |
| 4 | 3 3 4 5 5 6 7 9 |
| 5 | 1 1 $n$ 6 |
| 6 | 0 5 8 |
| 7 | 0 1 |

If the range and the interquartile range of the distribution are 42 and 18 respectively, what are the values of $m$ and $n$?
questions.answer:
Range: $71 - (20 + m) = 42 \Rightarrow m = 9$.

With 24 scores, $Q_1$ is the average of the 6th and 7th scores $= \dfrac{38 + 38}{2} = 38$, so $Q_3 = 38 + 18 = 56$.

$Q_3$ is the average of the 18th and 19th scores: $\dfrac{(50 + n) + 56}{2} = 56 \Rightarrow n = 6$. **(D)**

questions.question:
A ball is shot vertically into the air from the ground. The height of the ball above the ground, $h$ metres, can be modelled using the function $h = 20t - 5t^2$, where $t$ is measured in seconds. The graph of the height of the ball during its flight time is shown below.

For how many seconds is the height of the ball at least half its maximum height?
questions.answer:
The maximum is at $t = 2$ (the axis of symmetry, halfway between the zeros $t = 0$ and $t = 4$): $h = 40 - 20 = 20$ m.

Half the maximum is 10 m: $20t - 5t^2 = 10 \Rightarrow t^2 - 4t + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 2 \pm \sqrt2$.

Time at or above 10 m $= (2 + \sqrt2) - (2 - \sqrt2) = 2\sqrt2 \approx 2.8$ s. **(C)**

questions.question:
Box A contains 3 red balls and 2 white balls while box B contains 6 red balls and 1 white ball.

John draws a ball randomly from box A and then puts it into box B. If John draws a ball randomly from box B afterwards, what is the probability that John draws a red ball?
questions.answer:
Box B then holds 8 balls.
- Red moved ($\frac35$): B has 7 red, $P(\text{red}) = \frac78$.
- White moved ($\frac25$): B has 6 red, $P(\text{red}) = \frac68$.

$$P(\text{red}) = \frac35 \times \frac78 + \frac25 \times \frac68 = \frac{21}{40} + \frac{12}{40} = \frac{33}{40}. \quad \textbf{(C)}$$

questions.question:
A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 is shown.

| $n$ | 2% | 3% | 4% | 5% | 6% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.020 | 2.030 | 2.040 | 2.050 | 2.060 |
| 4 | 4.122 | 4.184 | 4.247 | 4.310 | 4.375 |
| 6 | 6.308 | 6.468 | 6.633 | 6.802 | 6.975 |
| 8 | 8.583 | 8.892 | 9.214 | 9.549 | 9.898 |
| 10 | 10.950 | 11.464 | 12.006 | 12.578 | 13.181 |

An annuity account is opened and equal contributions are made at the end of each 6-month period for 4 years.

For the first 4 years, the interest rate is 6% per annum, compounding half-yearly. After the 4 years the investor no longer makes contributions.

For the 5th year, the interest rate increases to 7% per annum, compounding annually. The amount in the account at the end of the 5th year is \$14 271.66.

What contribution is made during the first 4 years?
questions.answer:
First 4 years: 8 periods at 3%, factor 8.892, so after 4 years the account holds $8.892X$.

The 5th year adds 7% once: $8.892X \times 1.07 = 14\,271.66 \Rightarrow X = \dfrac{14\,271.66}{9.51444} = \$1500$. **(A)**

questions.question:
Claire's laptop consumes 0.15 kilowatts of electricity per hour when charging. On average, she charges the laptop for 3 hours each day at a rate of 23.17 cents per kilowatt hour.

What will be the cost to charge her laptop for the month of September?
questions.answer:
September has 30 days.
$$\text{Energy} = 30 \times 3 \times 0.15 = 13.5\text{ kWh}$$
$$\text{Cost} = 13.5 \times \$0.2317 = \$3.13$$

questions.question: A person stands on level ground, 45 m away from the base of a 22 m high flagpole. Find the angle of elevation of the top of the pole, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: $$\tan\theta = \frac{22}{45} \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{22}{45}\right) \approx 26^\circ$$

questions.question:
A company hires electric bicycles to tourists. Company A charges according to $C = 24h + 18$, where $C$ is the total cost (dollars) and $h$ is the number of hours hired. The graph for Company B passes through the points $(0, 42)$ and $(6, 150)$.

Determine the equation representing Company B.
questions.answer:
Gradient $= \dfrac{150 - 42}{6 - 0} = 18$, intercept 42:
$$C = 18h + 42$$

questions.question: On the Cartesian plane above, graph the equation representing Company B.
questions.answer: Draw the straight line through $(0, 42)$ and $(6, 150)$. It meets Company A's line at $(4, 114)$.

questions.question: Using the graph, or otherwise, determine the number of hours for which the two companies charge the same amount.
questions.answer:
$$24h + 18 = 18h + 42 \Rightarrow 6h = 24 \Rightarrow h = 4\text{ hours}$$
(Both charge \$114.)

questions.question: A family plans to hire bicycles for 7 hours. Which company should they choose? Justify your answer using calculations.
questions.answer:
- Company A: $C = 24(7) + 18 = \$186$
- Company B: $C = 18(7) + 42 = \$168$

They should choose **Company B**, which is \$18 cheaper.

questions.question:
A sports nutrition company mixes three ingredients, electrolytes : water : flavouring in the ratio $5 : 3 : 2$. A production batch contains 450 L of water. The finished drink is bottled into 600 mL bottles.

Determine the maximum number of full bottles that can be filled.
questions.answer:
Water is 3 parts, so 1 part $= 150$ L and the batch is $10 \times 150 = 1500$ L $= 1\,500\,000$ mL.
$$\frac{1\,500\,000}{600} = 2500\text{ bottles}$$

questions.question:
Meri hopes to have \$36 000 in 5 years' time to buy a car. She opened a savings account today which pays interest of 4% p.a. compounded half-yearly.

Calculate the minimum single sum of money that Meri needs to invest today to ensure she reaches her savings goal.

Sivani attended a cocktail party. After drinking for 3 hours ($H$), she consumed 4 standard alcoholic drinks ($N$). When she stopped drinking, Sivani calculated that she needed to wait 4.5 hours ($T$) before she would reach zero blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

Sivani used the following formulas for her calculations.
$$\text{BAC} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M} \qquad \text{and} \qquad T = \frac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$$

What was Sivani's mass to the nearest kilogram?

Tina has 4600 shares in a company and received a total of \$483 in dividends. At the time the shares were valued at \$5.60 each.

What was her dividend yield?
questions.answer:
Dividend per share $= \dfrac{483}{4600} = \$0.105$.
$$\text{Dividend yield} = \frac{0.105}{5.60} \times 100\% = 1.875\%$$

questions.question:
A painting was purchased for \$2500 and depreciated in value over six years as shown in the graph below.

Determine the number of years it will take for the painting to reach a salvage value of \$100.
questions.answer:
The graph is a straight line (straight-line depreciation) falling from \$2500 to \$1000 in 5 years, i.e. \$300 per year.
$$2500 - 300n = 100 \Rightarrow 300n = 2400 \Rightarrow n = 8\text{ years}$$

| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |

Show that Jordan's taxable income is \$58 540.

Jordan's financial information for the 2025–26 financial year is shown below.

| Description | Amount (\$) |
|---|---|
| Wages | 61 200 |
| Overtime payments | 1 450 |
| Bank interest earned | 520 |
| Work-related deductions | 4 250 |
| Charitable donations | 380 |
| PAYG tax paid | 9 130 |

| Taxable income | Tax payable |
|---|---|
| \$0 – \$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4 288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |

Determine if Jordan receives a tax refund or must pay additional tax. How much is his refund or liability? Justify your answer with calculations.

questions.question:
The diagram is a semicircle, radius 5 cm, with another, smaller semicircle cut out.

Find the perimeter of the shaded diagram, correct to one decimal place.
questions.answer:
- Large arc: $\frac12 \times 2\pi \times 5 = 5\pi$
- Small arc (diameter 5 cm, radius 2.5 cm): $\frac12 \times 2\pi \times 2.5 = 2.5\pi$
- Straight edge: 5 cm
$$P = 5\pi + 2.5\pi + 5 \approx 28.6\text{ cm}$$

questions.question:
The distances covered by 240 male athletes in two fitness tests are normally distributed. The mean and standard deviation for each fitness test is displayed in the table below.

| | Test 1 | Test 2 |
|---|---|---|
| $\bar{x}$ | 1680 m | 1760 m |
| $\sigma$ | 150 m | 125 m |

The coaching staff classify performance more than two standard deviations above the mean as outstanding.

James covered a distance of 2000 m in both test 1 and test 2. He claims that he performed outstandingly in both tests. Is James correct? Justify your answer using appropriate calculations.
questions.answer:
$$z_1 = \frac{2000 - 1680}{150} \approx 2.13 > 2 \quad \text{(outstanding)}$$
$$z_2 = \frac{2000 - 1760}{125} = 1.92 < 2 \quad \text{(not outstanding)}$$
James is **not** correct: only his Test 1 result is outstanding.

questions.question:
Janie buys a used car for \$8640.

To transfer the registration to her name it will cost a transfer fee of \$32 plus \$3 per \$100 or part thereof on the sale price of the car.

How much will it cost for Janie to transfer the car to her name?
questions.answer:
$\$8640$ is 87 lots of \$100 or part thereof.
$$\text{Cost} = 32 + 87 \times 3 = \$293$$

questions.question:
She needs to pay \$547.00 for insurance, and she also wants to have personalised number plates which cost \$220 to order, plus an annual fee of \$102, all payable at the time of ordering.

If she has \$10 000 in her bank account, will she have enough to cover the total cost of the car including the transfer of registration? How much short or over is Janie? Justify your answer with calculations.

A gift box of height 8 cm is shown below.

The cross-section of the box is a regular polygon, with each vertex 10 cm from the cross-section centre.

What is the volume of the box, in cubic millimetres, correct to two decimal places?
questions.answer:
The cross-section is a regular pentagon: 5 congruent triangles with two sides of 10 cm and an included angle of $\frac{360^\circ}{5} = 72^\circ$.
$$A = 5 \times \tfrac12 \times 10 \times 10 \times \sin 72^\circ \approx 237.7641\text{ cm}^2$$
$$V = Ah = 237.7641 \times 8 \approx 1902.1130\text{ cm}^3$$
$1\text{ cm}^3 = 1000\text{ mm}^3$, so $V \approx 1\,902\,113.03\text{ mm}^3$.

questions.answer:
Using Kruskal's algorithm (shortest edges first, skipping any that form a cycle):

Would it be appropriate to use the line of best fit to estimate the number of coffees sold on a day when the average temperature is 9°C? Give a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: No. 9°C is far outside the data range (21°C to 32°C), so this is extrapolation; the line even gives a negative number of coffees ($N \approx -1$).

questions.question:
Two hundred tickets are sold in a raffle in which there are two prizes. Amanda purchased five tickets in the raffle. The first ticket drawn wins the first prize, while the second ticket drawn wins the second prize.

Complete the tree diagram by including the missing probabilities. Calculate the probability that Amanda wins at least one of the prizes.
questions.answer:
Tree diagram ($W$ = Amanda wins, $\overline{W}$ = does not win):
- First prize: $P(W) = \frac{5}{200}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{195}{200}$
- After $W$: $P(W) = \frac{4}{199}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{195}{199}$
- After $\overline{W}$: $P(W) = \frac{5}{199}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{194}{199}$

$$P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\overline{W}\,\overline{W}) = 1 - \frac{195}{200} \times \frac{194}{199} = \frac{197}{3980} \approx 0.0495$$

questions.question:
The network diagram below shows the baggage collection system at an airport. Suitcases arrive at the Baggage Claim Hall and must reach the Arrivals Exit. The points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$ are sorting and transfer areas, and 10 conveyor belts operate between the points. The numbers on the conveyor belts represent the maximum number of suitcases per minute that can be transported along each conveyor belt.

What is the capacity of Cut 1 shown on the network diagram?
questions.answer:
Cut 1 crosses $E \to$ Exit (85), $C \to$ Exit (60) and $B \to D$ (45). ($D \to C$ crosses back from the sink side, so it is not counted.)
$$\text{Capacity} = 85 + 60 + 45 = 190$$

questions.question:
The network diagram below shows the baggage collection system at an airport. Suitcases arrive at the Baggage Claim Hall and must reach the Arrivals Exit. The points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$ are sorting and transfer areas, and 10 conveyor belts operate between the points. The numbers on the conveyor belts represent the maximum number of suitcases per minute that can be transported along each conveyor belt.

Draw the minimum cut on the network diagram.
questions.answer: The minimum cut crosses $A \to E$ (70), $\text{Hall} \to C$ (65) and $B \to D$ (45), with capacity $70 + 65 + 45 = 180$.

questions.question:
The network diagram below shows the baggage collection system at an airport. Suitcases arrive at the Baggage Claim Hall and must reach the Arrivals Exit. The points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$ are sorting and transfer areas, and 10 conveyor belts operate between the points. The numbers on the conveyor belts represent the maximum number of suitcases per minute that can be transported along each conveyor belt.

What is the maximum number of suitcases that can pass through the airport per minute?
questions.answer: Maximum flow $=$ minimum cut $=$ **180 suitcases per minute**.

questions.question:
The network diagram below shows the baggage collection system at an airport. Suitcases arrive at the Baggage Claim Hall and must reach the Arrivals Exit. The points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$ are sorting and transfer areas, and 10 conveyor belts operate between the points. The numbers on the conveyor belts represent the maximum number of suitcases per minute that can be transported along each conveyor belt.

The airport would like to increase the maximum number of suitcases that can flow through the airport. Suggest a change that the airport could make to one of the conveyor belts to allow for an increase of 5 suitcases per minute.
questions.answer: Increase the capacity of a belt in the minimum cut by 5, e.g. $A \to E$ from 70 to 75 (or $\text{Hall} \to C$ from 65 to 70, or $B \to D$ from 45 to 50).

questions.question:
A wildlife sanctuary is breeding an endangered species of turtle. The population is modelled by the equation
$$P = 150(1 + r)^t$$
where $r$ is the annual rate of population increase and $t$ is the number of years since the beginning of 2020.

How many turtles were there at the beginning of the program?
questions.answer: At $t = 0$: $P = 150$ turtles.

questions.question:
A wildlife sanctuary is breeding an endangered species of turtle. The population is modelled by the equation
$$P = 150(1 + r)^t$$
where $r$ is the annual rate of population increase and $t$ is the number of years since the beginning of 2020.

By the end of 2025, the population of the turtles was 338. What was the annual percentage rate of increase in the population of turtles from the beginning of 2020 to the end of 2025? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
questions.answer:
The end of 2025 is $t = 6$.
$$338 = 150(1 + r)^6 \Rightarrow 1 + r = \left(\frac{338}{150}\right)^{1/6} \approx 1.1450 \Rightarrow r \approx 14.5\%$$

questions.question:
A wildlife sanctuary is breeding an endangered species of turtle. The population is modelled by the equation
$$P = 150(1 + r)^t$$
where $r$ is the annual rate of population increase and $t$ is the number of years since the beginning of 2020.

To prevent overcrowding, the sanctuary plans to release 120 turtles into the wild at the beginning of 2028. Determine how many turtles will remain in the sanctuary immediately after the release.
questions.answer:
The beginning of 2028 is $t = 8$.
$$P = 150(1.145)^8 \approx 443 \Rightarrow 443 - 120 \approx 323\text{ turtles}$$

questions.question:
A surveyor measured the cross-section of a stormwater drainage channel. The estimated cross-sectional area is 23.1 square metres using three applications of the trapezoidal rule.

Determine the distance $x$ m between each survey point. Show all working.
questions.answer:
Depths are 0.4, 2.8, 3.6 and 0 m.
$$A \approx \frac{x}{2}\left(0.4 + 2 \times 2.8 + 2 \times 3.6 + 0\right) = \frac{x}{2}(13.2) = 6.6x$$
$$6.6x = 23.1 \Rightarrow x = 3.5\text{ m}$$

questions.question:
The diagram below shows the location of three cities and the airline routes connecting them.

City $H$ is 860 km from city $G$ on a bearing of $110^\circ$. City $F$ is 730 km due south of city $G$.

Find the distance, correct to the nearest km, and the bearing, correct to the nearest degree, of city $F$ from city $H$.
questions.answer:
$\angle FGH = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$.

**Distance** (cosine rule):
$$FH^2 = 860^2 + 730^2 - 2(860)(730)\cos 70^\circ \approx 843\,059 \Rightarrow FH \approx 918\text{ km}$$

**Angle at $H$** (sine rule):
$$\frac{\sin \angle GHF}{730} = \frac{\sin 70^\circ}{918.18} \Rightarrow \angle GHF \approx 48.3^\circ$$

**Bearing:** the bearing of $G$ from $H$ is $110^\circ + 180^\circ = 290^\circ$. $F$ is $48.3^\circ$ anticlockwise from that direction:
$$290^\circ - 48.3^\circ \approx 242^\circ$$

$F$ is about **918 km from $H$ on a bearing of $242^\circ$**.

questions.question:
A chocolatier melts a solid cylindrical block of chocolate with radius 9 cm and height 33 cm. The melted chocolate is moulded into 1160 identical solid chocolate spheres. All the chocolate is used in the manufacturing process.

Calculate the radius of each chocolate sphere, correct to one decimal place.
questions.answer:
$$V_{\text{cylinder}} = \pi(9)^2(33) = 2673\pi \approx 8397.6\text{ cm}^3$$
$$\frac43\pi r^3 = \frac{2673\pi}{1160} \Rightarrow r^3 = \frac{3 \times 2673}{4 \times 1160} \approx 1.7282 \Rightarrow r \approx 1.2\text{ cm}$$

questions.question:
A small business borrows \$65 000 to purchase new airport baggage handling equipment. The loan is taken out over a period of 5 years at a reducible rate of 6% p.a. charged monthly.

Repayments, $R$, are made monthly. Using the table of present value interest factors below and the recurrence relation
$$A_{n+1} = A_n(1 + r) - R,$$
calculate how much interest has been charged on the loan after the second repayment.

**Present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1** (interest rate per period)

| Period | 0.5% | 1% | 2% | 4% | 6% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The classification of bags at the airport is as follows:

| Weight of bag $W$ kg | $W < 14$ | $14 \le W \le 32$ | $W > 32$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classification | small | medium | large |

The airport manager knows that 15.866% of bags weigh more than 28 kg. (A standard normal table giving the area to the left of each $z$-score is provided.)

Calculate the value of $\sigma$.
questions.answer:
$P(W > 28) = 0.15866 \Rightarrow P(Z < z) = 0.84134 \Rightarrow z = 1$.
$$1 = \frac{28 - 20}{\sigma} \Rightarrow \sigma = 8$$

The table below lists activities for the construction of a community sports pavilion. Some durations are unknown (marked ?).

| Activity | Prerequisites | Duration (days) |
|---|---|---|
| A | – | ? |
| B | – | 6 |
| C | A | ? |
| D | B | 9 |
| E | A, D | 7 |
| F | C, E | ? |
| G | D | ? |
| H | F, G | 4 |

The minimum completion time for the project is 32 days. The critical path includes B, D, E, F and H only. The float time for activity G is 5 days, and the float time for activity C is 4 days.

Find the durations (in days) for activities F and G. Include a network diagram in your answer.
questions.answer:
Network: Start $\to$ A, B; A $\to$ C, E; B $\to$ D; D $\to$ E, G; C, E $\to$ F; F, G $\to$ H $\to$ Finish.

Critical path B–D–E–F–H: $6 + 9 + 7 + F + 4 = 32 \Rightarrow F = 6$.

H starts on day $32 - 4 = 28$. G can start on day $6 + 9 = 15$, and with 5 days of float: $15 + G + 5 = 28 \Rightarrow G = 8$.

The minimum completion time for the project is 32 days. The critical path includes B, D, E, F and H only. The float time for activity G is 5 days, and the float time for activity C is 4 days.

Find the range of durations possible for activities A and C, assuming whole number durations.
questions.answer:
F starts on day $15 + 7 = 22$. C has 4 days of float, so $A + C + 4 = 22 \Rightarrow A + C = 18$.

A is not critical, so A must finish before E's earliest start of day 15: $A \le 14$. Every duration is at least 1 day.

So $1 \le A \le 14$ and $C = 18 - A$, giving $4 \le C \le 17$.
